overview: BedWalker clears the client-side sleeping state every pre-motion tick while the player is in bed: it calls mc.thePlayer.stopSleeping() and closes the sleep GUI, so the client stops rendering the sleep screen and the player can look around and move - without ever sending the C0BPacketEntityAction STOP_SLEEPING that vanilla's Leave Bed button emits. The server therefore still believes the player is asleep, and vanilla's NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer pins a sleeping player back to its stored position and returns early, so the client-side freedom never becomes server-side displacement on a vanilla server. The module is a 24-line onPreMotion override with no settings and no packet logic of its own.

sections.p: onPreMotion checks mc.thePlayer.isPlayerSleeping() and, while true, calls stopSleeping() followed by displayGuiScreen(null). The vanilla wake path is entirely bypassed: GuiSleepMP's Leave Bed button sends C0BPacketEntityAction with Action.STOP_SLEEPING so the server clears its sleeping flag; BedWalker never sends that packet, so the server-side flag persists. Client-side, stopSleeping() clears the sleeping flag and sleep timer and resets the client's position to its current coordinates, and closing the GUI re-enables input and camera control.

Vanilla NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer contains a sleeping-player branch (around line 282): if the server-side player is sleeping, it runs onUpdateEntity, resets the player to the stored last position via setPositionAndRotation, updates the entity, and returns - discarding the incoming movement entirely. The moved-too-quickly check later in the same method explicitly exempts sleeping players (d15 > 0.0625 && !isPlayerSleeping()), and the teleport check does the same. So on an unmodified server, the client's C03 movement stream is ignored and the player is pinned at the bed: BedWalker's effect is visual and client-side freedom, not displacement.

The anticheat layer largely inherits the vanilla exemption. NCP's MovingListener early-returns for sleeping players in two places (onPlayerMoveMonitor: player.isDead() || player.isSleeping(); and the main move check with token 'sleeping', resetting sfHoverTicks), so SurvivalFly and MorePackets never see the moves. Hawk's movement checks guard on !p.isSleeping() (Fly, FastFall, FlyOld), skipping sleeping players outright. Arc v2 is the exception: its moving checks contain no sleeping exemption at all, so Flight and MorePackets evaluate the stream regardless - though on a vanilla-pinned server there is no displacement for them to measure, only the client's discarded C03s.

files.label: BedWalker.java
files.explanation: The module is one onPreMotion override: if the player is sleeping, it calls mc.thePlayer.stopSleeping() and mc.displayGuiScreen(null) every tick. No settings, no state, no packets of its own - the entire effect is clearing the client-side sleeping flag without sending the C0BPacketEntityAction STOP_SLEEPING the vanilla wake path would send, leaving the server to keep pinning the player to the bed while the client is free to look around and move.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement envelope, sleeping exemption)
countering.explanation: NCP's SurvivalFly rebuilds the client's movement envelope from the world, but it never sees a sleeping player's moves: MovingListener early-returns on player.isSleeping() both in onPlayerMoveMonitor and in the main move check (which resets sfHoverTicks and sets token 'sleeping'), so the check is not even invoked. The honest counter is vanilla itself - NetHandlerPlayServer.processPlayer's sleeping branch pins the player to the stored bed position and returns before any movement processing - so on NCP servers BedWalker's client-side freedom is enforced against by the server's own position reset, not by the anticheat.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement rate, sleeping exemption)
countering.explanation: NCP's MorePackets check rate-limits the movement packet stream against cc.morePacketsEPSMax with burst handling, but it is invoked from MovingListener's move pipeline after the sleeping early-return, so a player the server believes is asleep contributes no moves to the rate counters at all. BedWalker sends no packets of its own - it only lets the vanilla client resume its normal C03 stream - so there is nothing extra for the rate check to see. The enforcement that does exist is the vanilla processPlayer pin, which discards every C03 while the sleeping flag is set.

countering.label: Flight (vertical envelope, no sleeping exemption)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Flight check evaluates every move packet's vertical speed against ascend/descend ladders, max jump height, hover time and ascend distance - and unlike NCP and Hawk, Arc's moving checks contain no isSleeping/isPlayerSleeping exemption anywhere in the codebase, so the check runs even on a player the server believes is asleep. On servers that do not pin sleeping players (custom sleep handling, or servers that process movement before the sleep branch), BedWalker's resumed C03 stream is scored like any other movement, and any vertical gain while 'sleeping' trips the envelope. On vanilla-pinned servers the moves are discarded before Arc's packet hook sees displacement, which is the honest boundary of the check.

countering.label: FastFall (descending motion, sleeping guard)
countering.explanation: Hawk's FastFall check flags fall speeds beyond terminal velocity, but its guard list explicitly exempts sleeping players (pp.getPlayer().isSleeping() alongside teleport-accept, knockback, flying and swimming). The exemption is the module's cover on Hawk servers: BedWalker's whole premise is that the client moves while the server-side sleeping flag is set, and every Hawk movement check that could measure that motion - FastFall, Fly, FlyOld - carries the same !isSleeping() guard, so the resumed C03 stream is never scored. Only a Hawk configuration that removes the sleeping exemption, or a server that clears the sleeping flag, would bring the check to bear.
